chunks: Humayd ibn Ziyad from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Mithamī from Aban from Zurara from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said:

The prevented one slaughters where he was prevented, and his owner returns and goes to the women, and the confined one sends his sacrificial animal and appoints them a day, so when the sacrificial animal arrives, this one frees himself from Ihram in his place.

I said to him, 'What do you think if they return his dirhams and do not slaughter on his behalf, and he has already freed himself and gone to the women?' He said, 'Let him repeat, and there is nothing upon him, and let him refrain from the women now when he sends (the animal).'

key_terms.الْمَحْصُورُ: The confined one (one confined by illness or other valid excuse)
key_terms.الْمَصْدُودُ: The prevented one (one prevented by an enemy or obstacle from completing Hajj)

ai.seo_question: What is the difference in ruling between a prevented pilgrim and a confined pilgrim regarding their sacrificial animal and marital relations?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi distinguishes between the 'prevented' (masdūd) and 'confined' (maḥṣūr) pilgrim, establishing that the former must slaughter their offering at the site of prevention while the latter may send their sacrifice ahead. Notably, it clarifies that if the sent offering is rejected or not slaughtered, the pilgrim incurs no penalty and may resume marital relations, reflecting the Shia juristic emphasis on ease and the absence of compulsion in cases of valid impediment.

en.hubeali:
Humeyd Bin Ziyad, from Al Hassan Bin Muhammad Bin Sama’at, from Ahmad Bin Al Hassan Al Maysami, from Aban, from Zurara, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘The prevented one should slaughter (his sacrificial animal) where he has been prevented, and he would return, and he can go to the women. And the one confined (by an illness) should send his sacrificial animal, and they would appoint a day. So when the sacrificial animal reaches (its destination), this one would free himself from his Ihraam in his place’.

I said to himasws, ‘What is yourasws view if they were to return the Dirham back to him and they do not slaughter on his behalf, and he has already freed himself from his Ihraam, and has gone to the women?’ Heasws said: ‘So let him repeat, and there would be nothing (expiation) upon, and let him refrain from the women now, when he sends (his sacrificial animal)’.
en.sarwar: 9. Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd has narrated from al-Hassan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama‘ah from Ahmad ibn al-Hassan al-Mithamiy from Aban from Zurarah who has said the following: “Abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘

Al-Masdud (prevented) offers an animal for slaughtering wherever he is prevented and returns home. Women are lawful for him. Al-Mahsur (confined) sends his offering, sets up a certain time and when the offering reaches its place, he in his place comes out of the state of Ihram.’

I then asked, ‘What happens if they returned dirham and did not slaughter, but he has come out of the state of Ihram and has gone with women? He (the Imam) said, ‘He must do it again; there is nothing on him but for now he must stay away from women when he sends his offering.’”
